title_candidates: Gemini 3.8 turns scripts into spoken scenes
Try Gemini 3.8 text-to-speech in your browser
summary: Google's Gemini 3.8 text-to-speech models can direct a narrator or stage a two-speaker scene. A browser playground makes them testable in 15 minutes.

primary_source.title: Gemini 3.8 text-to-speech says hello
primary_source.author: Leland Rechis and Alan Cowen, on behalf of the Gemini Audio Team
key_facts: Google introduced Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS for detailed creative direction and character design, plus Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS for higher-volume, lower-cost speech generation.
Flash TTS can create custom voices from natural-language descriptions across more than 100 languages and dialects, while Google also offers a library of more than 2,000 production-ready voices.
Both models support line-by-line performance direction, including pacing, acting cues, dialect shifts, nonverbal sounds, and listener interjections.
Google says the models can maintain voice quality and character consistency across long audio and stage two-speaker conversations from a single script.
Generated audio carries a SynthID watermark.
Voice replication starts from a 30-second sample that the user owns or has permission to use and requires a matching verbal consent recording from the voice owner.
Both models are available in Google AI Studio and through the Gemini API; Flash TTS is also rolling out in Gemini Notebook, while Flash-Lite TTS is rolling out in Google Vids.
Google says AI Studio voice replication is unavailable in Illinois, Texas, the EEA, the UK, Switzerland, and India.

quote_candidates.text: every audio clip generated by our Gemini Audio models is watermarked with SynthID.
quote_candidates.position: Build with trust, consent, and transparency

supporting_sources.title: Gemini 3.8 TTS Playground
key_facts: Simon Willison published a browser playground for single-voice narration and multi-speaker conversations using the Gemini 3.8 TTS API.
The playground uses the reader's own Gemini API key and sends requests directly from the browser to Google's API.
The tool says the key remains in page memory, is excluded from shareable URLs, and is not saved to browser storage.
Willison reports that a 78-second two-speaker sample took about 20 seconds to generate with Flash TTS and cost roughly 2.74 US cents at the rates available when he tested it.

supporting_sources.title: Text-to-speech generation (TTS)
key_facts: Google's official guide documents single-speaker and multi-speaker audio generation and links to an interactive Google AI Studio test route.
The documented options include studio voices, a larger voice library, prompted voice design, and consent-gated voice replication.

supporting_sources.title: Gemini Developer API pricing
key_facts: Google currently lists a free tier for both Gemini 3.8 TTS models, with paid use metered separately for text input and audio output.
Google says free-tier content may be used to improve its products, while paid-tier content is not used for that purpose.

prerequisites: A Google account and a Gemini API key from Google AI Studio
A current JavaScript-enabled browser with audio playback
A short, non-confidential script you wrote or have permission to process

steps.instruction: Open [Google AI Studio's API-key page](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey), sign in, and create or copy a Gemini API key. Do not expose the key in a screenshot or use it on a shared computer.

Open the [Gemini 3.8 TTS Playground](https://tools.simonwillison.net/gemini-tts-playground), paste the key under Connection, and wait for the voice list to load. The third-party page says the key stays in page memory and requests go directly to Google's API.

Keep Single voice selected, choose Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS, select a built-in voice, and enter this original script: 'The museum closes in ten minutes. Please make your way to the main entrance, and thank you for visiting.' Add the delivery style 'calm, warm, and unhurried.'

Select Generate audio, then play the result under Listen. Check whether the words are complete, the pacing matches the direction, and the voice remains clear. Do not use voice replication for this test.

Switch to Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS, generate the identical script once, and compare clarity and delivery. Stop after the comparison, review current [API pricing and data-use terms](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing), and revoke the key in Google AI Studio if you do not plan to keep using it.

risk_flags: The Simon Willison playground is third-party software and requires the reader's own Gemini API key; the article must describe its direct-to-Google connection and key-handling claims precisely.
API pricing, quotas, and data-use terms can change; direct readers to the live pricing page rather than treating today's terms as permanent.
The practical guide uses a built-in voice only. Do not turn it into a voice-replication exercise.
Voice replication requires ownership or permission plus verbal consent and has regional availability restrictions.
The official announcement says some Gemini Notebook and Google Vids availability is rolling out, so do not present those destinations as universally available.
